<div class="info-card">

## How to Read the Axes

- **Horizontal Axis (X-Axis) — Observation Date Span Elapsed (Days Since First Sighting):**  
  Measures how many days have passed since that specific individual shark (or the Beaufort Sea mooring) was first recorded. Placing every track on a "Days Since First Sighting" scale lets us directly compare observation durations even when the recordings occurred in different calendar years.
- **Vertical Axis (Y-Axis) — Cumulative Spotting / Tracking Count:**  
  Counts each new detection in chronological order ($1, 2, 3, \dots, N$). A steep upward curve means frequent detections over a short period, while a flatter curve means detections were spread out over a longer time span.
- **Color Grouping:**  
  Dark teal points represent **Whale Shark Trackings (Coral Sea)** and light blue points represent **Beluga Whale Detections (Beaufort Sea)**.

</div>

<div class="info-card">

## Using the Interactive Controls

- **Top Filter Sliders & Dropdown:** Filter the points in real time by elapsed days, cumulative spotting count, or select a single named Whale Shark or the Beluga Whale dataset.
- **Timeframe View Menu (Top-Left of Plot):** Switch between the full 4,006-day span, a log-scale X-axis that spreads short and long tracks evenly, or zoomed-in views of the 0–400 day overlap window.
- **Bottom Range Slider:** Drag the handles at the bottom of the plot to zoom dynamically into any window of elapsed days.

</div>
